findings.reason: The protected source is already the canonical linear solution. It excludes bulls during the aligned scan, counts only unmatched decimal digits in two fixed arrays, intersects their frequencies, and formats the required hint directly. Its structure and names are clear and conventional, so no candidate is justified.

The Reference preserves the bull and cow semantics including one-use duplicate matching, both source examples in order with full explanations, all three constraints, and accessible text equivalents of both source diagrams.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064356922. It and the app-local source have identical bull counting, mismatch bucket updates, per-digit minimum sum, and hint formatting; only the required class wrapper differs.

The former 1,024-digit tier exceeded the source maximum of 1,000. Legal 32/128/500-digit disjoint strings now span 15.625x and force complete unmatched-occurrence searches while remaining below the execution safety cap. The current source passes at +0.01 relative exponent and 1.00x largest ratio; a correct occurrence-marking search passes all outputs but fails only scaling at +1.21 and 203.79x.

The Approach derives the per-digit frequency minimum as both attainable and maximal, defines shared length n before the manifest bounds, and now separates repeated-digit reuse limits from the all-bull and disjoint-set extremes.

The hash-bound public Reference remains verified against its reviewed source evidence, preserving both examples and explanations, all three constraints, exact duplicate semantics, and informational equivalents for both source diagrams.
